blocks.why: Normal night before the sim — up at 06:15 local for an 08:00 report, no rush.
Straight to bed after the sim: the 02:00 report means tonight's sleep has to happen in the evening or it doesn't happen at all.
Blackout blinds on as soon as I'm home — pay back some of what the 01:40 departure cost.
Early night to build the tank for a 12-hour four-sector day off a 04:35 report.
Long one in my own bed — this is the last full night before an all-nighter finishing at 03:43.
Two hours banked before I leave, because the back half of this duty sits right in the 02:00–06:00 hole.
Home at 04:25 and straight down; waking mid-morning so I can still get a proper night tonight.
Full anchor night on the day off — the one real reset before a 12-hour day and a midnight report.
Short turnaround at home after a 23:49 finish; asleep within fifteen minutes of walking in.
Sleep taken in the afternoon and evening because report is 00:35 tonight — treat this as the main sleep, not a nap.
Post-night sleep at home, capped early afternoon so I can still sleep tonight before the sim.
Back onto a normal night ahead of the 08:00 sim.
First of two clean nights off — let it run long, no alarm.
Second day off, holding a normal London pattern rather than drifting late.
Standard night before the sim day.
Bed at 20:00 local straight after the sim — 05:05 report means this is a short, protected window.
Ten hours after a 10h35 duty, loading up for tomorrow's 13-hour finish at 04:29.
Nap before the 15:25 report so the BCN turn at 02:54 local isn't flown on eighteen hours awake.
Six hours on landing, deliberately short so I'm sleepy again by nine tonight for the 06:50 departure.
Second sleep on the day off to get the body clock back under an early report.
An hour on the sofa after the FRA turn — short enough that it won't wreck tonight.
Very early night: tomorrow starts at 04:35 and ends in the middle of the following night.
The most important sleep of the month — I get home at midday and go straight down, because report is 21:25 for an all-nighter.
Seven hours in a dark room after a 04:48 finish, alarm set to leave just enough time for the 14:50 report.
Home just after one, sleep through the morning — the day off starts whenever I wake up.
Second sleep on the day off, because tomorrow is a 04:35 report and a 12h51 duty.
Eleven hours with no alarm after the longest early of the week.
Short afternoon nap on the day off to bank sleep against tomorrow's 04:35 report.
Down before eight so the four-sector CDG day starts on something like a full night.
Forty-five minutes when I get in, no longer, so tonight still works.
Full night before the sim — I need to arrive at the 24th rested because the 25th and 26th are brutal.
Straight home from the sim and into bed at 17:30 local — report is 02:00 and there is no other sleep available.
Home at half four, asleep by five: report is 01:45 again and I've already been awake since half past midnight.
Let this one run eleven and a half hours — it's the first chance to unload two consecutive fourteen-hour days.
Ninety minutes before the 14:40 report because I woke at five and the duty runs to 19:19.
The reset night — back onto London hours for two sim days.
Normal night between sim details.
Down at nine for the 06:10 report on the last day of the month.
An hour when I get home to close out the month, then back to normal evenings.

conflicts.statement: The sim on 02/09 ends 16:00 local and the next duty reports 02:00 local on 03/09. The only sleep available is an evening block starting around 18:00 local, which falls in the evening wake-maintenance zone when it is physiologically hardest to fall asleep.
options: Ask crewing to swap the sim to a morning-only slot or move it off 02/09
Treat the 18:00–00:15 block as a formal 'sleep opportunity' and use a wind-down routine, blackout and no screens from 16:45
Report fatigue if you get less than about four hours before the 01:00Z report

conflicts.statement: Three duties in a row (03/09 report 02:00L, 04/09 report 04:35L and 12h01, 05/09 finishing 03:43L after 13h03) each cut into the 02:00–06:00 body-clock low with no full recovery night between them.
options: Request the 05/09 all-night pairing be given to another crew
Take the pre-duty nap on 05/09 as non-negotiable
Plan controlled rest in the cruise on the ARN sectors if the operator permits it

conflicts.statement: Off duty 14:33 local on 08/09, report 00:35 local on 09/09 — about 10h02 at home, and the whole duty runs through the worst of the night.
options: Ask for the 09/09 FRA night turn to be moved a day
Sleep in the afternoon/evening of 08/09 as planned rather than trying to nap after the duty
Flag to the operator that this rest period is being used as a sleep opportunity at the wrong circadian time

conflicts.statement: Two separate duties on 18/09: an early ARN return reporting 04:35 local and finishing 11:22 local, then an all-night FCO return reporting 21:25 local. About 10h03 between them, and the night's sleep is gone entirely.
options: Ask crewing to split these across two crew — this is the single worst day of the month
Protect the 13:00–19:30 local sleep absolutely: phone off, blackout, no errands
Consider calling fatigued before the second duty if the afternoon sleep does not happen

conflicts.statement: The all-night duty ends 04:48 local on 19/09 and the next duty reports 14:50 local the same day — roughly 10h02, of which perhaps 7h is usable sleep, and it is daytime sleep after a full night awake.
options: Request a later report on 19/09
Use blackout blinds and earplugs for the morning sleep and accept a later start to the day
Report fatigue if the morning sleep is broken

conflicts.statement: Sim ends 16:00 local on 13/09 and the next duty reports 05:05 local on 14/09, giving a sleep window of under eight hours that has to start around 20:00 local.
options: Move the sim earlier in the day
Accept a short night and take controlled rest in the cruise if permitted
Bank sleep on 11/09 and 12/09 in advance

conflicts.statement: 13h04 duty reporting 15:25 local and landing at 03:59 local, with the final BCN sector departing 02:54 local — the approach into LHR is at the circadian trough after a full waking day.
options: Take the planned pre-duty nap
Ask for the last sector to be re-crewed
Plan an in-seat rest split with the Captain on the outbound BCN leg

conflicts.statement: Sim on 24/09 ends 15:00Z, then 25/09 reports 02:00 local for 13h41, then 26/09 reports 01:45 local for 14h02 — two of the longest duties of the month back to back, both starting in the middle of the night, with only about 10h04 between them.
options: This is the strongest case on the roster for a swap — raise it with crewing well before the month starts
If it stands, sleep in the evening on both 24/09 and 25/09 as planned and do not schedule anything else on those afternoons
Expect to be at the limit on the 26/09 FCO sector and use controlled rest if available

conflicts.statement: Sim finishes 16:00 local on 24/09 and the duty on 25/09 reports 02:00 local — about 10h, all of it in the evening, before a 13h41 four-sector day.
options: Ask for the sim to be moved off 24/09
Leave the sim debrief promptly and be in bed by 17:30 local
Flag the sim-to-night-report transition to your fatigue safety group

conflicts.statement: 12h51 duty with four sectors reporting 04:35 local, which requires a wake-up around 03:05 — sleep before this start is almost always truncated.
options: Use the day off on 20/09 for a second, evening sleep as planned
Ask for a three-sector version of this pairing
Keep the day off on 22/09 completely clear for recovery

conflicts.statement: Sim/training rows show only an Off Duty time of 16:00 local and a duty length of 8h00, with no explicit report time; I have read the report as 08:00 local (07:00Z) by subtracting the duty length, with no reporting offset applied.
options: Confirm the sim report time with crewing or the training department
If the actual report is earlier, shift the preceding sleep block back by the same amount
